description: A dependency-free local website that brings the existing Personal Energy Waste Simulator to the browser with appliance management, energy and cost calculations, potential waste analysis, what-if simulation, waste scoring, comparison, recommendations, reports, and browser-local persistence.

services.name: Energy simulator website
services.description: Standalone dependency-free browser application served locally on localhost, with all calculations and state managed client-side.

questions.question: Which language should the energy simulator website use?

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Browser-native JavaScript with no runtime or package dependency beyond a modern browser.

questions.rationale: A plain JavaScript frontend is the simplest suitable local website implementation and avoids a build tool or dependency install.

questions.question: Which framework should the website use?
questions.rationale: The user prefers a simple dependency-free local web app with no external services.

questions.question: What features should the application include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Dashboard; add/list/edit/remove appliances; daily/monthly/yearly kWh and INR cost calculations; configurable tariff; potential waste analysis; what-if simulation; transparent waste score; appliance comparison; rule-based recommendations; report view and export/print; validation; browser-local persistence; responsive accessible UI; local localhost run instructions
questions.answer: Dashboard; add/list/edit/remove appliances; daily/monthly/yearly kWh and INR cost calculations; configurable tariff; potential waste analysis; what-if simulation; transparent waste score; appliance comparison; rule-based recommendations; report view and export/print; validation; browser-local persistence; responsive accessible UI; local localhost run instructions
questions.rationale: These capabilities preserve the existing console functionality while adding the requested website UI and local browser workflow.

questions.question: Which data stores does the website require?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use in-memory state and optional local file persistence without a managed datastore.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Managed object storage for files and media.

questions.rationale: The website needs no managed datastore; browser localStorage is sufficient for local persistence and keeps the app dependency-free.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to access application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before accessing application features.

questions.rationale: The app runs locally for one user and has no authentication requirement.

constraints: Software-only local website served on localhost
Dependency-free browser implementation using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and standard browser APIs
Preserve the existing Java simulator's formulas, rule-based behavior, and INR tariff semantics
No Azure services, external services, APIs, network calls, AI/ML, hardware, or database
Use browser-local persistence; data is local to the browser and not synchronized
Responsive, accessible UI with validation and clear estimate disclaimers
Do not implement the source code during this planning phase
Include local run instructions and verification coverage in the eventual implementation
